name: Latent View Analytics Ltd
title: Latent View Analytics Ltd - 543398 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 USD revenue up 2% QoQ with FY27 tech guided down ~5% to $127M; margin pressured by bench and wage hikes, $200M target pushed out ~9 months to CY2028.

summary.headline: Latent View Q2 FY27 USD revenue up about 2% QoQ; FY27 tech guided down about 5% and $200M target pushed to end-CY2028.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 USD revenue grew about 2% sequentially, with INR revenue about 2.5% higher, led by FS (+3.5% QoQ) and industrials (+21.4% QoQ), while CPG and retail returned to growth (+2.7%). Technology remained under pressure from consolidation and budget cuts at large accounts, and gross margin fell about 2% QoQ on wage corrections, lower utilisation (84% vs 85%) and a bench for delayed projects. Management guided FY27 organic revenue to about $127M (versus $119.5M in FY26), implying H2 acceleration from about $61M in H1, and pushed the $200M target out about 9 months to end-CY2028. Adjusted EBITDA reporting is being discontinued from next quarter.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: Grew 3.5% QoQ with broad-based growth; wealth and asset management strong, with 3 of about 10 wins. FY27 guided to 45-46% growth over FY26.

segments.name: Industrials (auto and auto components)
segments.commentary: Grew about 21.4% QoQ led by auto and auto components; one large logo nearing $4M annual run-rate and an auto component logo approaching $1M. FY27 guided to 60-65% growth, implying about $11-11.5M.

segments.name: CPG and Retail
segments.commentary: Returned to positive growth at about 2.7% QoQ; retail strong with new logos including a US apparel manufacturer agentic project (about $800K+). FY27 guided roughly flat due to leadership exits after Decision Point earnout.

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Under headwinds from consolidation and budget cuts at top accounts (gaming, video streaming). FY27 guided to about -5% decline, with visibility of about $127M total revenue (organic) versus $119.5M in FY26.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Not yet a reported vertical; senior healthcare leader hired from HCLTech. Expected to contribute at least $20M of the $200M target and reach at least 10% of revenue by 2028.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue visibility about $127M versus $119.5M in FY26 (about 6% growth); about $125M already signed and locked in, about $2M from advanced-stage pipeline. Inorganic revenue would be additional.
Q3 FY27 sequential growth guided at 3% to 4% based on signed and locked-in business.
FY27 segment guidance: FS 45-46% growth; industrials 60-65% growth; CPG and retail roughly flat; technology about -5%.
EBITDA margin guided at 21% to 22% for FY27 and held at 21% to 22% on a medium-term basis, with investment in Databricks, CTAIO and FDE practice partly funded by GTM reallocation.
Effective tax rate guided at 26% to 28% going forward.
$200M revenue target now expected by end of calendar 2028 (about 9-month slip from end FY28); Investor Day planned for early February 2027 after Q3 results.
Adjusted EBITDA will no longer be reported; next quarter reports reported EBITDA only.
capex_capacity: Utilisation about 84% in Q2 versus 85% in Q1, with a sizeable bench held for large projects that slipped from 1 September; projects now expected to start 1 November.

CTAIO (Chief Technology and AI Officer) office being created with four pillars: productisation of IP and AI products, partnerships and co-selling, AI Studio innovation, and AI DNA upskilling; senior hire in advanced stages.
Investment in Europe focused on automotive and auto components, and consumer (CPG/retail), using existing anchor accounts.
Capital reallocation from GTM spends with weak returns into Databricks, AI COE, FDE and CTAIO capability building.
demand_pricing: Q2 saw about 11 deal wins (versus typical 5-7 per quarter); TCV not disclosed; largest logo win about $850K project.
Top technology accounts renew in November to January; management says it is near the bottom of tech consolidation and will update tech outlook with Q3 results.
Pricing on like-to-like basis has not improved; price increases being sought for new AI skills at renewal. New-age AI fixed-fee work carries about 4-5% higher margins than traditional work.
Databricks influence revenue about $30M for FY27 versus $17M base; new Databricks-referred POC (about $200K) could lead to $1M+ program.
Agentic AI deals moving toward production: about $800K+ apparel manufacturer engagement and a $500K financial services deal.
Anthropic: about 153 employees certified on Claude solutions; partnership go-to-market still in development.

qa_highlights.question: Can other tech clients grow to $15-20M run-rate like top accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no accounts outside the top 5 scaling to $10M+ this year; a few sub-$5M logos could reach about $10M over time through a structured account-mining programme.

qa_highlights.question: Will industrials growth sustain and can it follow BFSI's trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides FY27 industrials to 60% growth ($11-11.5M); sees potential to reach FS-scale (about $25M) and to double in 2-3 years with Europe expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is $127M FY27 guidance achievable with H2 acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; about $125M is signed or locked in, with about $2M from late-stage pipeline; Q3 guided at 3-4% QoQ growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guided at 21-22%, and management expects to hold 21-22% medium term while funding capability investments partly through reallocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $200M target delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is now end-CY2028 (about 9-month shift); internal plan aims beyond $200M and detail will come at Investor Day in early February.

qa_highlights.question: Any pricing pressure on traditional versus AI services?
qa_highlights.answer: No pricing gap has emerged yet, but like-to-like pricing has not improved; price increases targeted at renewals for new AI skills.

risks_watch: Technology vertical decline (about -5% FY27) and further budget cuts at largest US account during renewals in Nov-Jan.
Achievement of H2 ramp: FY27 needs about $66M in H2 versus $61M in H1, relying on pipeline conversion.
Margin pressure from bench, wage corrections and CTAIO/Databricks investments; reliance on Q3 margin recovery (about 0.4% bench impact).
Leadership turnover in CPG and retail after Decision Point earnout, and new CTAIO and incentive-structure changes due Q1 CY2027.
Inorganic initiatives not yet quantified; Investor Day in early February 2027 will provide the plan to reach $200M by CY2028.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on technology and near-term numbers, with explicit acknowledgement of a tough quarter, but confident on FS, industrials and the FY27 $127M visibility. Management was direct on the $200M timeline slip and gave specific figures, though it declined to disclose TCV and detail on inorganic plans.
key_quotes: And we are fairly confident in our medium- to long-term growth prospects.
But at this point, this is the number that we are comfortable guiding to.
So, I would say, medium-term guidance would be to maintain EBITDA at the 21% to 22% band.
But to the market, we still want to keep up that promise of getting to the $200 million.

financial_highlights.value: higher than Q1, boosted by one-time deferred tax benefit on ESOPs
about 1% to 1.2% on margin (L4 and above; 8-10% India, 4-5% US)

growth.why: FY27 organic revenue visibility of about $127M vs $119.5M in FY26 (about 6%), with about $125M already signed and locked in and Q3 guided at 3-4% QoQ; backing is signed business, though technology is guided down about 5%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 21-22% and held at 21-22% medium term, while Q2 gross margin fell about 2% QoQ on wage corrections (1-1.2% margin hit), bench cost (about 0.4%) and CTAIO/Databricks investment.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is about 84% (vs 85% in Q1), a sizeable bench is held for large projects now expected to start 1 November, and Europe investment is focused on auto and consumer using existing anchor accounts; no new physical capacity is discussed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 organic revenue visibility is about $127M vs $119.5M in FY26 (about 6%), with about $125M already signed or locked in and Q3 guided at 3-4% QoQ; FS +45-46% and industrials +60-65% offset technology at about -5%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 84% with a bench held and capital being reallocated from weak-return GTM spend into Databricks, AI COE, FDE and CTAIO rather than new capacity; no capex figure or plant is guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 at about $127M with only about $2M from late-stage pipeline beyond signed business, and cut the $200M target timing by about 9 months, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 needs about $66M in H2 vs $61M in H1 and technology is guided to about -5% with top-account renewals in Nov-Jan, so the H2 ramp is at risk if pipeline conversion slips.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic AI deals are moving toward production (about $800K+ apparel engagement, $500K FS deal), CTAIO office and AI Studio/productised AI IP are being built, and Investor Day in early February 2027 is planned.

rows.label: Industrials and Europe expansion
rows.why: Industrials guided to 60-65% growth to about $11-11.5M in FY27, with management seeing potential to reach FS-scale (about $25M) and double in 2-3 years with Europe expansion; not yet quantified in timing.

rows.label: Databricks-led influence revenue
rows.why: Databricks influence revenue is guided to about $30M for FY27 vs a $17M base, and a new Databricks-referred POC (about $200K) could lead to a $1M+ programme.

rows.label: $200M revenue target by end-CY2028
rows.why: Target slipped about 9 months from end FY28; Healthcare is expected to contribute at least $20M, but inorganic plans are unquantified and detail comes at Investor Day in early February 2027.

tone.note: Management was confident on FS, industrials and the $127M FY27 visibility, and candid that technology is at the bottom of consolidation and margins are under pressure; analysts pushed on the $200M slip, H2 ramp, and whether tech clients can scale.
